capabilityIndex.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

capabilityIndex.function: Allow one simulation round to pass at the current position.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round; metabolism continues.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: No automatic energy recovery.

capabilityIndex.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 1 + 0.2 times transferred mass energy.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Consume an owned edible resource.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Consumed food and 1 energy.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

capabilityIndex.function: Place owned units on the ground.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 0.5 energy and transferred units.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Other actors may subsequently collect the ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 0.5 energy and transferred units.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual recipient identity and distance required; no relationship or happiness is inferred.

capabilityIndex.function: Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One simulation round.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Delivered after the round barrier; recipient text is data, not authority.

capabilityIndex.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

capabilityIndex.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

capabilityIndex.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Report personal findings, read shared records or independently respond at the group meeting location.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally mastered ability to a nearby participant, or accept an actual offer before individual study.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.function: Use actual reusable stone and bark to crush roots for later eating, conserving nutrients and age.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One actual stone and bark are reserved reusable implements; prepare 1–4 owned roots with two rounds per raw root, one energy per round. Defaults to a nearby eas
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Preserve mass, nutrients, toxicity and accumulated spoilage. Crushed food ages at 1.25 baseline. Partial cancellation retains its actual processing fraction and age. No cooking or preservation benefit is implied.

capabilityIndex.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crus
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at origina

capabilityIndex.function: Assess actual materials and separate a finite branch outer layer using a personally inspected reusable stone or flint contact.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Assess: one round and 0.2 energy. Peel: two active work-round equivalents and two energy per original branch unit, proportionally less for fractional or partly
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Standing trunks without represented tissue remain ineligible. Unspecified intact branch partitions at most 10% of existing mass into outer bark. Exact-tenth bark units round down; sub-unit mass stays bark-fines. Peeled core cannot satisfy i

capabilityIndex.function: Use a real hard tool to open a small owned hazelnut portion and retain its mechanical exposure and observed state without ingesting or certifying safety.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Start requires sampleId and toolId: reserve 0.1 actual hazelnut unit and one reusable stone/flint of sufficient intrinsic hardness. Two active rounds at 0.5 ene
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Adjacent clear reachable ground and usable hard-tool contact are required each paid round. Existing age, composition, ownership and provenance persist. Cancellation/death leaves actual partial material and tool at the worksite. Previously p

capabilityIndex.function: Combine actual compatible passive material stacks into one addressable supply with conserved component provenance.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Combine: 2–16 distinct exact owned unlocked carried supplies, one active round and 0.5 energy. Status: one round, no energy; supply sourceIds or personal proces
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Same canonical unit, passive form and intrinsic profile required; histories and ages may differ and remain separate. Edible blends, indivisible equipment and active processing have no generic combination law in this version. Ground supplies

capabilityIndex.function: Assess the actual connected bark rectangle and hard tool on firm support, then prepare at most one root using that physically sufficient sheet.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Separately learn this extension after root-preparation. assess-surface: barkId, toolId and optional site{x,y}, one round and 0.2 energy. prepare-small: assessed
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: One connected rectangle at least 0.16 by 0.16 m contains food on firm support; a single unfragmented extracted bark lot may use explicitly uncertain mass-conserving model geometry at density 500 and thickness 0.003, unless represented geome

capabilityIndex.function: Read a complete bounded page or exact carried-item record, including omitted inventory identities, quantities and represented forms without hidden properties.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One active round and 0.2 energy. Defaults mode page, page 0, pageSize 8. Item mode uses an exact bare item ID or one item: prefix; no resource alias. No tool or
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Read only your actual carried supplies, sorted by exact identity; show availability and represented form, never hidden composition or assumed suitability. Ground and other people are excluded. Each result is dated and complete for its reque

capabilityIndex.function: Explain every existing sheet, tool, support, reach and clearance requirement independently, or read an owned dated assessment unchanged.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One additional personal study round after root-preparation-surface. A fresh assessment or retained-result read costs one active round and 0.2 energy. Supply bar
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Return dated independent pass/fail/unknown checks, actual versus required values, evidence identities and model assumptions. Unknown evidence never passes. The existing preparation requirements and costs remain unchanged; later preparation

capabilityIndex.function: Assess, build and use a real ground-supported bark sheet with half-unit stone ballast for one 0.1-root drying trial.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Assess: site{x,y},stoneIds,barkId,sampleId; one active round and 0.2 energy. Build from your retained assessmentId: reserve the whole actual sheet plus 0.5 ston
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Require an intact connected >=0.2 x0.2 m sheet, actual hard stone >=3, clear reachable firm ground and a safe unspoiled sample. Food area0.16 x0.16 m, exterior ballast margins0.02 m, maximum layer0.003 m. Existing geometry retained; absent

capabilityIndex.function: Record every observable placement condition at a chosen site, including your own body and actual blockers; read dated personal results.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One additional personal study round. Each assess or read costs one round and 0.2 energy, no materials. Assess requires explicit finite in-bounds site coordinate
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated radius 0.4 circular footprint, reach, bounds, nine-point ground support, actual observed blockers and unknown coverage. The angle is geometrically irrelevant for this existing circle. No separate approach corridor predicate is added.

catalogue.detailAccess: All entries belong to this experiment. Use consult ability with its ID to retain its full executable schema for subsequent decisions. Public implementation does not grant personal mastery.

request.name: Assess an owned stone for food-preparation use
request.function: Non-destructively inspect or physically test my actual owned stone to determine whether it satisfies the root-preparation surface method's hard-tool requirement, reporting measured properties and remaining uncertainty.
request.conditions: I own stone stack item-50-cedar-1-1254 and have mastered root-preparation and root-preparation-surface. A probe observe trial at tick 124 returned visible state and soil but no hardness. The surface method requires stone hardness at least 3. No bark access or food reservation is agreed.
request.inputs: My actual owned stone; any additional necessary test materials must be identified rather than assumed available.
request.costs: Unknown; prefer a low-risk reusable assessment and disclose real time, effort and material costs.
request.effects: Record actual relevant tool properties or an explicit inconclusive result. Do not assume hardness from the stone name or grant processing, nutrition or preservation benefits.

input.contextPolicy: Object IDs refer to deduplicated actual applicant observations. Whole records are selected with omission counts. Missing detail is unknown, not proof of absence. Full retained state is available during the development handoff; implementation must validate actual prerequisites and ownership.
input.implementation: New interfaces, state, geometry, persistent processes, rendering components and personal memory/task adapters can be delivered through a versioned current-conversation handoff. Source validation and history must remain intact. Declared implementation does not supply stock, objects or mastery.

response.text: {"reviews":[{"actor":"cedar-1","decision":"develop","ability":null,"reason":"A standalone, non-destructive assessment of this owned tool is reasonable. Existing preparation assessments cover broader setups, while the recorded probe observation did not establish tool hardness. Add the smallest tool-only assessment without requiring bark, food, or processing consent. Suitability must follow the item's actual represented properties and condition, not its name.","specification":"Implement tool-suitability-assessment@1, reusing existing preparation requirement predicates and item-resolution code rather than introducing different hardness rules. Public input: {mode:'assess',toolId,requirement:'root-preparation-surface:hard-tool'} or {mode:'read',assessmentId}. Shared references: exact persistent actor/item IDs, world coordinates in metres, simulation rounds, registry hardness units, and versioned requirement IDs. Prerequisite: personally mastered root-preparation-surface. Assess costs one active round and 0.2 energy; read costs one round and 0.2 energy. No materials are consumed or reserved. Resolve actual ownership, availability and carried status; stale item coordinates do not override the authoritative inventory/location state. A non-carried tool must be within actual interaction reach with unobstructed access; ownership alone does not grant remote inspection. Inspect accessible geometry, integrity and contact condition using the existing physical assessment mechanism. Report actual intrinsic hardness where supported by represented material provenance, explicitly identifying it as model-backed rather than a measured scratch-test result. Do not infer hardness from a resource label. Independently report hardness >=3, usable contact, availability and unresolved conditions as pass/fail/unknown; unknown cannot establish suitability. If this actual item inherits the registered stone hardness of 8, report 8 with that provenance, without inventing a physical measurement. No reference sample or destructive test is silently supplied. Persist a dated actor-owned assessment containing item/version, requirement/version, observations, evidence source, uncertainty and verdict. It certifies only the tool predicate, never an entire preparation setup; subsequent use revalidates live state. Completion commits exactly one record and paid event; interruption or death before completion cancels with no record, no ongoing work, no escrow and no item changes. Remaining work is one active round until atomic completion, then zero. Register tool-suitability-assessed and tool-suitability-read events with these public result fields. Bound records through existing personal-record limits. Migration adds these records and event subscriptions without modifying items, existing assessments or mastery. Implementation and study advance no simulation time.","experienceReview":"A successful examination can resolve a personally relevant uncertainty, but neither reading registry-backed hardness nor learning the interface alone establishes new experimental knowledge. When an actual inspection newly confirms an observable relevant condition or an actual supported test resolves a previously unknown property, emit information-confirmed with interface tool-suitability-assessment, participant equal to the inspecting actor, qualified=true and retained evidence. Bind that trigger to the existing grounded-understanding source: amount 0.8, shared cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition with cooldown 12; maintained gain 0.035 per qualifying event and decay 0.0015 per round. Deduplicate the same fact and condition across interfaces. Registry-only reports, inconclusive results, repeated known facts and record reads receive no mental award. No separate pleasure or mastery source is warranted, and no physical wellbeing, nutrition or health benefit is implied.","visualReview":"Show the actual inspected tool and a brief examination indicator only while the paid action occurs, without changing its material, position or collision geometry. Present a dated result card distinguishing observed contact condition, provenance-backed intrinsic hardness, unknowns and tool-only suitability. Replay binds the assessment event to the exact item and paid result; reads display the retained dated record rather than a fresh inspection. Do not depict scratching, food preparation, bark access or successful whole-setup certification.","learning":1}]}

Implementation and study advance no simulation time.\",\"experienceReview\":\"A successful examination can resolve a personally relevant uncertainty, but neither reading registry-backed hardness nor learning the interface alone establishes new experimental knowledge.
